input: Schedule swim lessons for the toddler

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The toddler's age and swimming ability determines which lesson level or program type to look for — parent-child classes vs. independent beginner lessons vary significantly by age.
Whether a provider has already been shortlisted or the search is starting from scratch changes whether the next step is researching options or directly booking.
The city or neighborhood determines which facilities (pools, YMCAs, private instructors) are realistically accessible.
Budget per lesson or per session affects whether private instruction, semi-private, or group classes are on the table.
Available days and times for the family directly filters which programs are even schedulable — some pools only offer weekday mornings, others weekend slots.
Whether the parent wants to be in the water with the child (parent-child class) or prefers instructor-only lessons shapes the type of program to target.
Knowing the goal — water safety, comfort in water, or competitive stroke development — determines what to prioritize when evaluating programs.

gold.taskTitle: Schedule swim lessons for the toddler
gold.taskDescription: Find and book swim lessons for a toddler, covering everything from choosing a provider to confirming enrollment.

questions.title: How old is your toddler, and can they swim at all?
questions.description: Determine the child's age and current swim ability to identify the right lesson level — parent-child, beginner, or another tier.

questions.title: Do you have a pool or provider in mind already?
questions.description: Establish whether the task starts at the research stage (finding options) or the booking stage (enrolling in a known program).

questions.title: What city or neighborhood should the lessons be near?
questions.description: Pinpoint the location to surface relevant and accessible facilities — YMCA, community pool, private swim school, etc.

questions.title: What is your budget per lesson or per session?
questions.description: Clarify the financial limit to filter between group classes, semi-private, and private instruction options.

questions.title: Which days and times work best for your schedule?
questions.description: Identify available time slots to immediately rule out programs that don't align with the family's weekly availability.

questions.title: Do you want to be in the water with your child?
questions.description: Determine whether the family prefers a parent-child participation class or an instructor-led independent lesson format.

questions.title: What is the main goal — safety, comfort, or stroke skills?
questions.description: Understand the primary outcome the family wants so the right program emphasis can be matched when comparing providers.
